title: Cap. III Rat. 9: glory depending on others' sins needs foresight — Stephen's martyrdom
pass_a_gloss: Reason 9. To those whose glory depends on the sins of others, it cannot be decreed except from foresight: as for example, because the glory of Stephen somehow hung upon the impiety of the Jews who were about to stone him, God could not decree glory to him, at least not in that degree in which it was to be given by so glorious a martyrdom, except with the sin foreseen which furnished occasion for his martyrdom, and at the same time with his patience and faith foreseen by which mediating from their cruelty he acquired for himself the outstanding glory of martyrdom. If not therefore to all, yet at least to some glory is destined from foresight of merits.
pass_b_english: Rat. 9. Where someone's glory hangs on others' sins, they say it cannot be decreed except from foresight. Take Stephen: his glory somehow depended on the impiety of the Jews who would stone him — so God could not decree him glory, at least not in the degree that so glorious a martyrdom would give, unless that sin (which occasioned the martyrdom) was foreseen, and with it his patience and faith, by which he won outstanding martyr's glory from their cruelty. So if not to all, at least to some glory is destined from foresight of merits.
source_text: Rat. 9. Quorum gloria dependet ex peccatis aliorum, iis non potest decerni nisi ex praevisione: ut verbi causa, quia gloria Stephani aliquo modo pendebat ex impietate Judaeorum qui illum erant lapidaturi, non potuit Deus gloriam illi decernere, saltem non in eo gradu quo tam glorioso martyrio danda fuit, nisi praeviso peccato quod occasionem praebebat ejus martyrio, et simul praevisa ejus patientia et fide quibus mediantibus ex illorum crudelitate eximiam martyrii gloriam sibi acquirebat. Si non omnibus ergo, at aliquibus saltem destinatur gloria ex praescientia meritorum.
